text:
A muscle fibre relaxes when the nerve stimulus is removed: the motor neuron stops firing, acetylcholine is cleared from the neuromuscular junction, and the fibre is no longer excited. SERCA then pumps calcium back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, so tropomyosin blocks the myosin-binding sites on actin again. A forceful stimulus produces stronger contraction or tetanus, not relaxation.

CONFIDENCE: 90
